summary.headline: Sell narrow, measurable SME automation as a service before building another SaaS.
summary.best_opportunity: Productized AI workflow automation for one UK SME niche
summary.why_now: Live search surfaced GOV.UK AI adoption reporting dated July 2026 and a 2025 Small Business Britain/BT survey describing enthusiasm alongside adoption barriers; that supports a practical implementation offer, not a claim that every firm is ready to buy.

top_opportunities.name: Niche SME workflow automation retainers
top_opportunities.description: Audit and automate one repetitive workflow for a defined niche (for example enquiry triage, quote follow-up or document processing), then provide monitoring and small monthly improvements.
top_opportunities.why_now: UK adoption signals show interest but real barriers; a fixed-scope, human-reviewed delivery offer reduces implementation friction. Evidence is directional rather than proof of willingness to pay locally.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small service firms and professional practices with repetitive admin and an owner-manager buyer.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 for hosting, automation tools, API usage, insurance and basic outreach; can stay below £2,000.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–4 weeks with direct outreach and a paid pilot.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Strong: £150–£600/month monitoring, support and iteration after a setup fee.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong for a solo software engineer; technical delivery and lightweight integrations are core skills.
risks: SMEs may lack clean processes or data; scope tightly and require a human approval step.
AI/automation competition is growing and measurable client savings must justify the retainer.

scores.demand: 4/5, adoption reporting indicates a real but uneven market

top_opportunities.verdict: Best near-term bet: pre-sell one workflow and charge for implementation before productising repeatable pieces.

top_opportunities.name: Local-business website care and conversion service
top_opportunities.description: Build or improve a fast, accessible website with enquiry forms, booking, analytics and local search basics, then provide hosting, updates and lead-conversion reporting.
top_opportunities.why_now: Live search surfaced a GOV.UK Small Business Survey 2025 report and current business-website coverage, but no robust primary evidence in this run on unmet website demand; validate in a specific local trade niche.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades, clinics and other local firms with outdated or poorly converting sites.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£700 for hosting, templates, domains and outreach.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks; deposit-funded build is straightforward to sell through local prospecting.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Moderate: £40–£200/month for maintenance, hosting and conversion tweaks.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong; web engineering maps directly, with sales and copywriting the main gap.
risks: Crowded, price-sensitive market; differentiate by vertical and booked-lead outcomes.
Clients may treat maintenance as optional unless value is reported clearly.

scores.demand: 3/5, plausible local need; limited direct evidence gathered

top_opportunities.verdict: Fastest simple cash offer if sold as a niche outcome and not as generic web design.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry and quote follow-up automation for trades
top_opportunities.description: Implement a lead-capture, response-time, quote reminder and review-request workflow integrated with the firm's existing inbox or CRM.
top_opportunities.why_now: The offer addresses a concrete revenue leak rather than selling AI novelty; live UK search found broad SME digitalisation signals, but no specific measured lost-lead benchmark, so validate with interviews.
top_opportunities.buyer: Plumbers, electricians, roofers and other local trades receiving enquiries across calls, forms and email.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£500 for CRM/automation subscriptions, hosting and a demo setup.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks with a paid setup pilot.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Strong: £100–£350/month for workflow monitoring, tuning and reporting.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong; integrations and lightweight dashboards suit software skills.
risks: Access to customer data and messaging consent must be handled correctly.
Small firms may not have enough lead volume to value an ongoing service.

scores.demand: 3/5, commercially plausible but not quantified in gathered sources

top_opportunities.verdict: Good narrow offer: sell response-time and follow-up outcomes, not a generic chatbot.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical lead-generation website with paid qualified enquiries
top_opportunities.description: Create a focused local landing site and search/content funnel for a high-value service category, then sell verified enquiries to one or more providers.
top_opportunities.why_now: Can start cheaply and produce recurring buyer payments, but the live search research did not establish keyword volumes or acquisition costs; treat it as a test, not dependable immediate income.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local providers in high-value, underserved service categories.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,000 including site, tracking and small paid-search experiments.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 4–12+ weeks; depends on ranking or paid acquisition and buyer agreements.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Potentially strong with repeat lead buyers, but only after proving lead quality and volume.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technically; requires consistent sales, content and channel experimentation.
risks: SEO can take months and paid lead costs can exceed the sale price.
Lead quality, privacy and transparent consent create operational obligations.
top_opportunities.verdict: Only pursue after validating buyer willingness to pay and a low-cost acquisition channel.

top_opportunities.name: Micro-SaaS for a repeated operational pain in one vertical
top_opportunities.description: Turn a repeated, validated spreadsheet or admin workflow into a small subscription tool, initially onboarding customers manually and automating only common steps.
top_opportunities.why_now: UK SME AI adoption and digitalisation signals suggest ongoing workflow change, but market-wide signals do not validate a particular product; customer discovery must precede build.
top_opportunities.buyer: A tightly defined business niche with recurring admin work and a reachable community.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,500 for development services, hosting, payments and initial customer discovery.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 4–12+ weeks; slower than service-led offers unless pre-sold.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High potential subscription revenue, but uncertain until retention is demonstrated.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong technical fit; distribution and support are the main risks.
risks: Building before securing paying design partners wastes time.
Incumbents can bundle similar features and churn may be high.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not start with a broad SaaS build; extract a product only after repeated paid service engagements.

best_pick.name: Niche SME workflow automation retainers
best_pick.why_it_wins: A paid implementation can generate near-term cash while a support retainer builds recurring revenue. It fits solo engineering, costs little to test, and current UK AI adoption research suggests both interest and adoption friction—making a narrow, outcome-led service more credible than speculative SaaS.
validation_plan: Choose one accessible niche and interview 10 owner-managers about one repetitive workflow, its frequency, current cost and existing tools.
Offer a fixed-price pilot to 3 qualified prospects; proceed only if at least one pays and the result can be measured.
best_pick.first_offer: A 10-day workflow audit and implementation for £500–£1,000, followed by optional £200/month monitoring and improvements; quote only after defining a bounded process.
best_pick.mvp: One trigger, one integration and one human-reviewed outcome (such as sorting inbound enquiries and drafting replies), with logging, exception handling and a basic monthly impact report.
customer_types: Small professional-service firms handling repetitive inbound enquiries
Local service businesses with manual quoting, scheduling or document admin
best_pick.do_today: Pick one niche, list 30 nearby prospects, send 10 personalised messages offering a short process audit, and book discovery calls before building a demo.
